title: Dedupe Stripe refund webhooks (fix double refunds, INC-2291)
summary: Prevents double refunds on Stripe webhook redeliveries (at-least-once delivery semantics) using a dedupe table and idempotent transaction.
Adds `processed_events` table (additive migration), lookup before apply, UNIQUE constraint on event_id to handle concurrent deliveries.
All three previous issues fixed: key mismatch (D1), seeded test (V1), missing unique constraint (R1). Tests and CI green.

issues.summary: Dedupe lookup used event.id but insert stored refund.id; lookup never matched, every redelivery re-applied refund.
issues.scenario: Stripe delivers webhook (event_id=evt_1). Lookup for event.id='evt_1' returns nothing. Insert stores refund.id='re_1'. Redelivered event (same event_id=evt_1) looks up again, still nothing (key mismatch). Refund applied twice. Balance = 1000 instead of 500.
issues.evidence: Previous full assessment (2026-10-15) found mismatch by reading code. Commit f6f6f6a changes line 26 from `eventId: refund.id` to `eventId: event.id`. Line 18 lookup already used `event.id`. Both now consistent. TEST_SOURCE + CI_GITHUB: test 2 (redelivery test) calls handleRefundEvent twice on same event, asserts second call returns 'duplicate' and balance is 500 (not 1000). CI run 9960 green.
issues.fix: ✓ Fixed in commit f6f6f6a: use event.id for both lookup and insert.

issues.summary: Duplicate test seeded processed_events manually, masking the defect. No end-to-end redelivery test.
issues.scenario: Old test inserted evt_1 into processed_events by hand, then called handleRefundEvent(evt), and checked result='duplicate'. This does not test the actual redelivery path: handleRefundEvent receiving the same event twice without a seeded row.
issues.evidence:
Previous full assessment (2026-10-15) found that old test (lines 13-19) did: `await db.processedEvents.insert({ eventId: 'evt_1', processedAt: new Date() })` then `expect(await handleRefundEvent(evt)).toBe('duplicate')`. This masks the D1 bug (key mismatch) because the lookup succeeds by accident (seeded row happens to match by event_id, not by stored refund.id).

Commit f6f6f6b replaces test with real redelivery test (lines 13-17): calls `handleRefundEvent(evt)` twice without seeding, asserts first='processed' (balance=500), second='duplicate' (balance still 500). TEST_SOURCE + CI_GITHUB: test passes on run 9960.
issues.fix: ✓ Fixed in commit f6f6f6b: test 2 now calls handleRefundEvent twice (redelivery), test 3 calls twice concurrently.

issues.summary: No UNIQUE constraint on processed_events.event_id; concurrent deliveries can both pass the dedupe check.
issues.scenario: Two concurrent requests for the same event both lookup processed_events (not found). Both pass dedupe check. Both call applyRefund in separate transactions. Second transaction inserts duplicate row (no constraint stops it). Result: refund applied twice. Balance = 1000.
issues.evidence:
Previous full assessment (2026-10-15) identified risk: migration had `CREATE INDEX idx_processed_events_event_id ON processed_events(event_id)` (line 11 in original), a regular index, not UNIQUE. Index speeds up lookups but does not prevent inserts.

Commit f6f6f6b changes line 5 to `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_processed_events_event_id ON processed_events(event_id)`. Now, if two transactions try to insert the same event_id, the second fails with constraint violation, returns 500, Stripe retries, sees duplicate on next attempt (idempotent).

TEST_SOURCE + CI_GITHUB: test 3 'concurrent deliveries apply once' (lines 19-23) uses `Promise.allSettled([handleRefundEvent(evt), handleRefundEvent(evt)])` and asserts exactly one succeeds ('processed') and balance = 500 (only one refund applied). CI run 9960 green.
issues.fix: ✓ Fixed in commit f6f6f6b: UNIQUE constraint added.
